svg.title: Emergency-only stopped rabbit snare
svg.desc: A four-panel working card for a life-threatening Victorian survival emergency. Panel A gives the strict entry gate and exact materials. Panel B diagrams a passive free-running stopped brass-wire snare with a ten centimetre loop, a fourteen centimetre stop measurement, a smooth eye, tether, peg and nine centimetre set height. Panel C shows a clear rabbit run, rejected sites, marking and hourly inspection. Panel D routes a non-target animal to cautious release and a positively identified European rabbit to the separately warned Australian humane-dispatch and death-confirmation sequence. The card is not an ordinarily lawful Victorian trap design and remains unapproved.
svg.text: RABBIT SNARE — EMERGENCY GATE
WORKING CARD · PANEL A OF 4 · VICTORIA
LIFE-THREATENING EMERGENCY ONLY
Food must be needed to protect life or prevent really serious injury before rescue.
Rescue · first aid · warmth · shelter · water · findability remain first.
Not for practice, ordinary hunting, convenience or hunger alone.
WORKING, UNAPPROVED METHOD
95% source-match of priority/legal warning · 70% source-match of dimensions
55% Victorian completeness/effectiveness · 40% written novice dispatch.
Editorial estimates—not probabilities of capture, legality, safety or survival.
ALL MUST PASS BEFORE SETTING
□ Human-life threshold + only reasonable food route in time
□ European rabbit evidence here; no non-target sign
□ Stay at the safe waiting place; remain awake and close
□ Exact materials · hourly checks · release + dispatch ability
One NO / UNKNOWN on the method gates = DO NOT SET.
EXACT KIT — NO VALIDATED SUBSTITUTE
3–4-strand brass rabbit wire, doubled to 6–8 at noose · smooth running eye
fixed stop · rot-proof cord · firm peg · notched support · marker · cutters
No fishing line, string, plant fibre, spring pole, drag or self-locking loop.
READ ALL 4 PANELS · ORDINARY VICTORIAN USE IS NOT AUTHORISED HERE
BUILD A FREE-RUNNING STOPPED LOOP
WORKING CARD · PANEL B OF 4 · PANEL A CONTROLS
PASS PANEL A FIRST. THIS RESTRAINS; IT MUST NOT BE USED TO STRANGLE.
Improvised design lacks Victoria's ordinary-use spring, two swivels and prescribed hardware.
10 cm open loop diameter
smooth running eye
fixed stop
14 cm measured along moving wire
from eye to stop — not diameter
rot-proof tether
firm peg
MAKE + TEST
1 Pass free wire through smooth eye. Pull smaller; release.
2 Crimp stop 14 cm along moving wire. Shape 10 cm loop.
3 Secure wire → rot-proof cord → peg. Keep tether clear.
Must relax; stop + peg must hold. Any bind, kink or fray = STOP.
PANEL A GATE CONTROLS · DO NOT USE THIS DETACHED PANEL ALONE
SET, MARK AND WATCH
WORKING CARD · PANEL C OF 4 · PANELS A–B CONTROL
USE: OPEN RABBIT RUN
9 cm
Short vegetation · several fresh rabbit signs
Loop across centre · support releases freely
REJECT THE SITE
× Burrow mouth or fence gap
× Waterhole or gully crossing
× Road, public track or camp
× Pet or livestock route
× Tree, root, rock, scrub or drop
× Native-animal or hare sign
No entanglement, suspension,
drowning or weather exposure.
SET ONLY DURING A SHORT, AWAKE WATCH
1 Clear the whole tether radius. Drive peg nearly flush. Do not use a drag.
2 Mark + number the set. Record location and time. Start with one.
3 Watch from a distance when possible. Physically inspect at least HOURLY.
4 Check at once after weather, animal noise or line movement.
5 Remove before sleep, movement, lost inspection ability or rescue.
Hourly is a conservative project limit—not a capture or welfare guarantee.
EVERY SET MUST BE FOUND AND REMOVED · READ PANEL D BEFORE SETTING
CAPTURE: ACT NOW
WORKING CARD · PANEL D OF 4 · PANELS A–C CONTROL
APPROACH QUIETLY · LONG SLEEVES / GLOVES · FACE CLEAR OF TEETH + CLAWS
A snare is not selective. Identify the animal before choosing the next branch.
WRONG ANIMAL — RELEASE, DO NOT EAT
If apparently uninjured and release is safe: hold the line away from your body
with a long forked stick; cut the NOOSE ITSELF so no loop remains; step back.
Unsafe release: back away; protect people. 000 is only for immediate human danger.
Otherwise seek vet / wildlife rescue / land manager. Do not invent a killing method.
EUROPEAN RABBIT — DISPATCH NOW
UNDER 1 kg + already proficient: hold both hind legs, head down. Place neck at
skull base between two fingers; push down while stretching neck/head backward.
OVER 1 kg OR UNKNOWN: one heavy, sharp blow with solid blunt bar to back of
skull immediately behind ears; immediately complete neck dislocation above.
Failure sign? Repeat stun + dislocation AT ONCE. Kicking alone may be involuntary.
Confirm ALL: no rhythmic breathing · no eye blink/reflex · fixed glazed eyes ·
pale mouth tissue that does not regain colour after brief pressure.
40% confidence that text alone enables humane novice use. Training is required.
CAPTURE ≠ SAFE FOOD
Poison, illness, carcass, dressing and cooking gates still control. Remove all sets.
NOT FIELD-APPROVED · NOT ORDINARY HUNTING · COMPLETE METHOD + REVIEW STILL REQUIRED
